clue.text: White object cut on record

indicators.note: in an across clue 'on' places the clipped piece after the record

parts.note: an album is a record, an LP

indicators.note: cut tells us to clip the last letter off the word for object

parts.note: an end is an aim or object

explanation.surface: Someone describes a white item lying on top of a vinyl disc.
explanation.definitionFit: Albumen is egg white, the clear protein that turns white when cooked.

clue.text: Shade by golden stream

parts.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold
a burn is a Scottish word for a stream

explanation.surface: Shade from the sun beside a gleaming brook.
explanation.definitionFit: Auburn is a reddish-brown colour, a shade usually used of hair.

clue.text: Onset of battle quick, brisk

indicators.note: onset means the beginning, so take the first letter

parts.note: racing means going fast, quick

explanation.surface: The opening of a fight is fast and vigorous.
explanation.definitionFit: Bracing describes something invigorating, like a brisk fresh wind.

clue.text: Vegetable order directed at unwelcome bloke?

parts.note: a bloke is a man
get out is the command you give an unwanted visitor

explanation.surface: A vegetable shouts at an unwanted man to leave.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as a shout: 'Man, get out!'
explanation.definitionFit: Mangetout is a pea eaten pod and all, a type of green vegetable.

clue.text: Shortage of work on the radio

indicators.note: on the radio means the word is heard, not seen

parts.note: to knead is to work dough

explanation.surface: A broadcast reports a lack of jobs.
explanation.definitionFit: Need means lack or want, a shortage of something required.

clue.text: Parlour worker to regret retiring on the whole

indicators.note: in an across clue 'on' puts the reversed piece after the first

parts.note: mass can mean the whole or the bulk, as in 'the mass of people'

indicators.note: retiring means drawing back, so the word for regret is read backwards

parts.note: to rue is to regret

explanation.surface: A massage-parlour employee is sorry to be leaving after all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Parlour' suggests a front room, but here it is a massage parlour.
explanation.definitionFit: A masseur works in a massage parlour, giving massages to clients.

clue.text: Pest confusing ones and noughts no good, passing wrong information

indicators.note: ones are the letter I and noughts the letter O, and confusing them swaps each one for the other in the pest's name

parts.note: a mosquito is an insect pest

explanation.surface: A computer bug muddles binary digits and wrongly reports the data.
explanation.walkthrough: In computing, ones and noughts are binary digits; here they stand for the letters I and O, which trade places in the pest's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Misquoting means repeating someone's words wrongly, giving out false information.

clue.text: Fracas would be delicious with my involvement

indicators.note: the answer plus the word my makes the word for delicious, so my is taken away from it

parts.note: scrummy is slang for delicious
taken as written: the word my

explanation.surface: A brawl would taste wonderful if I joined in.
explanation.walkthrough: SCRUM with MY attached would read SCRUMMY, British slang for delicious; so remove MY.
explanation.definitionFit: A scrum is a disorderly crowd or scuffle, a fracas.

clue.text: Nothing to impress me, lifting prohibition

indicators.note: in a down clue lifting means the whole string is read upwards

parts.note: O is the figure nought, nothing
to grab someone is to impress them
taken as written

explanation.surface: Nothing impresses me, says someone raising a ban.
explanation.definitionFit: An embargo is an official ban, especially on trade.

clue.text: Go on about English relative being rich

indicators.note: about means the word for go on surrounds the other pieces

parts.note: to go on is to rant, talk at length
a son is a relative

explanation.surface: Someone rants about an English relative who is wealthy.
explanation.definitionFit: Resonant describes a sound that is deep and full, rich in tone.

clue.text: Puzzle is hard? Not entirely occupying brother

indicators.note: occupying means the trimmed phrase sits inside the word for brother

parts.note: Brer is a dialect form of brother, as in Brer Rabbit

indicators.note: not entirely means the last letter of the phrase is dropped

parts.note: something that is hard 'ain't easy' in colloquial speech

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether a puzzle is tough, and says it only partly engages their brother.
explanation.walkthrough: Brer is the old Southern US dialect form familiar from Brer Rabbit; 'ain't easy' is the colloquial way of saying something is hard.
explanation.definitionFit: A brainteaser is a puzzle or problem designed to test the wits.

clue.text: Something caught under back

indicators.note: back means the word for under is read in reverse

parts.note: sub is a prefix meaning under, as in subway

explanation.surface: Something gets snagged beneath someone's back.
explanation.definitionFit: People speak of catching a bus, so a bus is something caught by travellers.

clue.text: Condition for invasion by a Viking

indicators.note: the condition is invaded, so the letter A goes inside it

parts.note: a rider is a condition added to an agreement or verdict

explanation.surface: A requirement that a Viking must invade first.
explanation.definitionFit: Vikings were seaborne raiders who attacked coasts across Europe.

clue.text: Practice session in Spooner's card game finished

indicators.note: Spooner's signals the opening sounds of the two words are swapped

parts.note: rummy is a card game
done means finished

explanation.surface: A rehearsal held during a card game that the Reverend Spooner has just completed.
explanation.walkthrough: Swap the opening sounds of RUMMY DONE to get DUMMY RUN; DONE is said 'dun', so the swap gives 'run'.
explanation.definitionFit: A dummy run is a trial or rehearsal carried out before the real thing.

clue.text: Less on top — nonsense!

parts.note: balder means having less hair on top
the printed punctuation mark is a dash

explanation.surface: Someone protests that the claim about thinning hair is rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: The dash in the clue is itself part of the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Balderdash is senseless talk, rubbish or nonsense.

clue.text: PM's address more absurd, hugged by silly person with nothing on

indicators.note: hugged by means the absurd word is held inside the word for silly person

parts.note: a goon is a silly or foolish person
dafter means sillier, more absurd
O is the figure nought, nothing
taken as written

explanation.surface: The Prime Minister's speech is even sillier, embraced by a naked idiot.
explanation.walkthrough: PM is not the Prime Minister but post meridiem, the afternoon: a greeting is an address.
explanation.definitionFit: Good afternoon is the greeting one uses in the PM hours, after noon.

clue.text: The cane demanded for this rude riposte?

definitions.meaning: a cane is a stem of this fruit plant, so the clue asks for the fruit
a rude noise made with the tongue as a retort

explanation.surface: Someone deserves a caning for a cheeky reply.
explanation.definitionFit: A raspberry is a fruit grown on canes and also a rude blowing noise of derision.

clue.text: Top rock music, seedy thing?

parts.note: a cap is a top or lid

indicators.note: rock means shake, so the following letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone asks if the best rock music is rather seedy.
explanation.definitionFit: A capsicum is a pepper, a fruit packed with seeds.

clue.text: Bird in wild dead in situ, having struck a pose

indicators.note: in means the bird is placed inside the rearranged letters
wild signals that the following letters are jumbled

parts.note: a tit is a small bird

explanation.surface: A bird out in nature lies dead where it fell, posed dramatically.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wild' scrambles DEAD IN SITU; TIT goes inside the result.
explanation.definitionFit: To attitudinise is to strike affected poses, so having done it means having posed.

clue.text: Run up German article as part of the deal

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the word is read upwards

parts.note: to dart is to run quickly
ein is the German word for a

explanation.surface: Someone runs up a German item as part of a business agreement.
explanation.definitionFit: A trade-in is goods handed over as part payment in a deal.

clue.text: Having cracked up, had elected prince

indicators.note: cracked means broken, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: in means elected, as a party voted in

explanation.surface: Someone who had gone mad was elected anyway.
explanation.walkthrough: The dauphin was the title of the eldest son of the King of France.
explanation.definitionFit: The Dauphin was the French crown prince, heir to the throne.

clue.text: Jill perhaps measures round two rivers

indicators.note: round means the measures go around the rivers

parts.note: feet are units of length, measures
R is the abbreviation for river, twice

explanation.surface: A girl called Jill measures the distance around two rivers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jill' looks like a girl's name, but a jill is a female ferret.
explanation.definitionFit: A jill is the name for a female ferret, so Jill is an example.

clue.text: Recognised colours

definitions.meaning: ... as an adjective means accepted, recognised as normal

explanation.definitionFit: Standard means generally accepted, and is also a military flag or set of colours.

clue.text: Animal eating beef finally put off

indicators.note: eating means the animal surrounds the letter

parts.note: a deer is an animal

indicators.note: finally means take the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: An animal chewing beef finally lost its appetite.
explanation.definitionFit: To defer is to postpone, to put something off until later.

clue.text: Wretched Tube, so slow

indicators.note: wretched suggests something wrecked, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone complains that the miserable London Underground is so sluggish.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tube is the London Underground railway.
explanation.definitionFit: Obtuse means slow-witted, dull in understanding.

clue.text: Holiday given up to lose a stone by the way

indicators.note: to lose means the letter A is removed
in a down clue given up means read upwards

parts.note: a break is a holiday
taken as written

explanation.surface: A holiday abandoned in order to shed a stone in weight, by the way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'given up' reverses BREAK to KAERB, and 'to lose' removes A. A stone here is not a weight but a kerbstone at the edge of the road.
explanation.definitionFit: A kerb is the stone edging alongside a road or pavement.

clue.text: Prompt line voiced

indicators.note: voiced means we hear the word spoken

parts.note: a queue is a line of people waiting

explanation.surface: An actor asks for a line to be spoken as a reminder.
explanation.definitionFit: A cue is a prompt, the signal given to an actor to speak or enter.

clue.text: One living in the Dark Ages more remote, burying dead

definitions.text: One living in the Dark Ages

indicators.note: burying means the word for dead is put inside the word for more remote

parts.note: farther means more distant or remote
late means dead, as in the late king

explanation.surface: Someone in a distant medieval past buries the dead.
explanation.walkthrough: The Dark Ages here is figurative: someone with hopelessly outdated beliefs.
explanation.definitionFit: A flat-earther clings to a disproved belief, metaphorically living in an unenlightened era.

clue.text: Butterfly cunning by day

parts.note: Mon is the abbreviation for Monday
arch means sly or cunning

explanation.surface: A butterfly is described as crafty in daylight.
explanation.definitionFit: The monarch is a large orange and black butterfly famous for migrating.

clue.text: Cry showing film, Lethal Weapon

parts.note: to bay is to howl or cry, as a hound does
on means showing, as a film on at the cinema
ET is the Spielberg film about an extra-terrestrial

explanation.surface: A shout announces that the film Lethal Weapon is screening.
explanation.walkthrough: Lethal Weapon looks like the film title, but read literally it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A bayonet is a blade fixed to a rifle, a deadly arm for close fighting.
